_comment: Shared recognition contract of the two mail gates (scripts/hooks/outgoing-copy-gate.py :: is_send_invocation and scripts/email-send-gate.mjs :: isSendInvocation). The conformance test (send-invocation-conformance.test.ts) runs EVERY case through BOTH implementations and asserts both equal `expected` -- divergence between the two copies surfaces as a test failure, not an incident (SUBGATEPOZ822, msg 14289). Unparseable-input fallbacks are deliberately NOT here: the two gates fall back differently by design (copy-gate: strong literals; hard-gate: full legacy patterns) and each pins its own in its scope test. A [marveen:...] prefixu esetek Marveen fuggetlen review-probai (store/marveen-send-gate-cases.json, msg 14302) -- a 'hatar' jeloles tortenete: az ot naiv exec-alak 2026-08-22 delutan LEZARULT (expected true), a megmaradt dokumentalt korlat az elfedett/futasidoben osszerakott kod; egy kesobbi valtozasnak itt teszt-hibakent kell jelentkeznie MINDKET iranyban, a nema atbillenes a tiltott allapot. INTERAGENTHOMOGLIF923 (2026-09-23): the inter-agent `curl .../api/messages` cases STAY expected:false here -- they are NOT email sends, and NONE of the email copy rules (accents, name rule, em dash) run on them. What changed is OUTSIDE this contract: the copy gate runs a SEPARATE, homoglyph-only check on that path (outgoing-copy-gate.py :: inter_agent_homoglyph_gate), blocking on a mixed-script word and passing an uninterpretable body with a loud warning. A reader must not take the expected:false rows as 'the path is unguarded', nor that change as 'the full copy gate now runs there'. #718: a case may carry `cwd` (relative to the repo root): the directory the command runs in, the hook payload's cwd; without it the test process's cwd (the repo root). #725 coarse (Marveen msg 14989, GO 14995): a command that names a send-capable token anywhere AND contains a hard construct (any heredoc but not a here-string, backslash-newline, an extglob paren, [[, case, a multi-line $( ) or backtick substitution) counts as a send, at depth 0, in both gates. Rows tagged "#725 coarse" are that deliberate over-block, including inter-agent posts built that way; text naming send tokens is written with the Write tool instead.
